families.summary: VMS+ (K173810, 2018) is a Windows-based adjunct analysis system that reconstructs 3D chamber models from freehand 2D ultrasound images tracked by a 6DOF magnetic tracker with ECG trigger, using a knowledge-based reconstruction (KBR) catalog of MRI heart-shape models; K173810 extended the RV-only predicate VMS (K150628) to LV, LA and RA volumes and ejection fractions with bench testing only. VMS+ 3.0 (K191493, 2019-10-16, product code LLZ; predicate GE EchoPAC K150085, reference VMS+ K173810) moved the KBR engine from an internet-accessed Windows server onto the local system, added touchscreen/medical-grade cart hardware, PACS send/retrieve, manual ED/ES frame selection and 3D-echo/MRI import, with bench testing and no clinical study. VMS+ 4.0 (K241222, 2025-02-26, product code QIH; predicate K191493) adds an AI-generated automated 'first guess' placement of anatomical control points that users must still adjust and confirm, plus magnet-free position sensors; the summary reports an internal user-validation study on 160 RV images (criteria met, proportions not reported), describes no clinical study, and explicitly states the accuracy of the AI initial point placement was not evaluated.
families.intended_use_quote: The VMS+ system is an adjunct to existing ultrasound imaging systems and is intended to record, analyze, store and retrieve digital ultrasound images for computerized 3-dimensional image processing.
families.indications_for_use_quote:
The VMS+ is an adjunct to existing ultrasound imaging systems and is intended to record, analyze, store and retrieve digital ultrasound images for computerized 3-dimensional image processing.

The VMS+ is indicated for use where Left Ventricle (LV), Right Ventricle (RV), Left Atrium (LA), and Right Atrium (RA) volumes and ejection fractions are warranted or desired.
embedded_ai_features: Knowledge-based reconstruction (KBR) of LV, RV, LA and RA 3D surfaces from tracked 2D echo landmarks against a catalog of heart models
Chamber volumes and ejection fractions for all four chambers; comparison table in K241222 (p.9) lists outputs as EDV, ESV, ejection fraction, stroke volume and cardiac output
Automated AI 'first guess' placement of anatomical control points on 2D images via a button press (K241222, VMS+ 4.0); user must manually adjust/confirm before reconstruction
Edge-detection refinement of user-placed control points to detected anatomical boundaries (K241222)
KBR engine runs locally on the system since VMS+ 3.0 (K191493); previously on a remote Windows server accessed over the internet

clearances.changes_summary: Expanded the predicate VMS (K150628; RV volumes and EF only) to LV, RA and LA volumes and ejection fractions by adding KBR heart catalogs for each chamber; same fundamental technology (freehand 2D scanning with 6DOF magnetic tracking, ECG trigger, video capture card, KBR database).

VMS+ 3.0. Primary predicate GE EchoPAC (K150085, PACS/LLZ); reference device VMS+ (K173810). Same KBR technology and IFU. Differences vs K173810: KBR located locally on the system instead of on a Microsoft Windows Server accessed over the internet; touchscreen and mouse input; touchscreen image capture/UI; medical-grade computer on a variable-height roll stand; user manually selects ED and ES frames (predicate auto-determined first ED frame); magnetic transmitter moved closer to the patient; scan-plane adjustment; PACS send and retrieve. Supported by software V&V and bench testing of volume accuracy vs the cleared VMS+; no clinical study.

clearances.changes_summary: VMS+ 4.0 (Traditional 510(k); summary dated 2025-01-17). Same IFU as VMS+ 3.0. The only software change is an additional, AI-generated method for placing the 'first guesses' of anatomical control points (button press), which users must still manually update to a final location before reconstruction; hardware change removes the magnet from the transmitter/sensor (magnet-free position tracking). Supported by bench testing, software V&V (basic documentation level), electrical safety/EMC, cybersecurity testing including external penetration testing, and an internal user-validation study on 160 RV images; verification tests were also performed against doctors' point placement. The summary describes no clinical study (it does not contain an explicit 'no clinical study' statement). Software may also be installed on a separate workstation to import 3D datasets, MRI studies and VMS+ studies.

training_data.description: K173810 summary describes KBR 'heart catalogs' of heart models but gives no catalog/training set size or source. Company product page states the KBR algorithm 'leverages a MRI shape catalogue and anatomical landmarks from standard 2D echocardiography'; the Ahmad 2022 abstract (PMID 36029116) describes 'a validated Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) database of normal ventricular and atrial morphologies'. Neither gives numbers. K241222 (VMS+ 4.0) describes the KBR as 'referencing a database of MRI heart shape catalogs' (p.5) and adds an AI-generated first-guess control-point feature, but gives no training set size, source or algorithm description for either the KBR catalog or the point-placement model. K191493 gives no training information. Peer-reviewed hint only: Sheehan 2010 (PMID 20346319) describes a KBR reference database of 54 TOF patients for MRI-based reconstruction; whether the cleared catalogs are the same or larger is not stated anywhere.

validation_data.description: FDA summary reports only bench testing of LV/LA/RA catalogs ('automated and manual testing to verify reconstruction accuracy'); no dataset size, no clinical study. K191493: bench testing of volume accuracy vs the cleared VMS+, no dataset size. K241222: internal user-validation study on 160 RV ultrasound images (users, patients, sites not stated); bench testing; 'verification tests ... against doctors' point placement' without reported results; no clinical study.

prior_validations.description: Predicate VentriPoint Medical System (K150628, 2015-05-22, IYN) cleared for RV volumes and EF; peer-reviewed 2D-KBR RV validations against CMR in TOF, PAH, d-TGA, adult CHD and sarcoidosis (2011-2022) listed under papers.

Sponsor-run comparison studies vs cMRI registered on ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT01419756 (repaired TOF, n=109, completed) and NCT01557582 (PAH, n=103, completed, primary endpoint mean VMS-cMRI percent difference within ±10% for RVEDV/RVESV).

Per openFDA, the VMS lineage is: VMS K140153 (2014-03-06, IYN), VMS K150628 (2015-05-22, IYN, RV only), VMS+ K173810 (2018-05-14, IYN, four chambers), VMS+ 3.0 K191493 (2019-10-16, LLZ) and VMS+ 4.0 K241222 (2025-02-26, QIH). K191493 and K241222 summaries are now extracted in this family. Company site markets VMS+ 4.0 as software installable on a personal workstation that builds 3D chamber models from 3D echo or MRI images using KBR.

Company press release (GlobeNewswire, 2026-08-12) reportedly describes a subscription model, a 2025 FDA clearance and a VMS+ 3.0 usability study (13 sonographers, 98% task completion). The release could not be retrieved in the verification session; the usability-study figures remain unconfirmed.

Company press release (TheNewswire, 2025-02-27) announcing FDA 510(k) clearance of VMS+ 4.0: cites 'AI-assisted automated point placement to improve user workflow efficiency', 'Magnet-free sensors enabling more efficient pairing and improved workflow', use 'for patients with cardiac pacemakers', prior clearance in the E.U., U.K. and Canada, and the vendor claim of volumes and EF 'with accuracy equivalent to MRI' (no study cited in the release).

papers.title: Accuracy of knowledge-based reconstruction for measurement of right ventricular volume and function in patients with tetralogy of Fallot.
papers.key_result: KBR algorithm applied to MRI images (not echo) in 20 repaired-TOF patients vs manual 3D tracing: EDV r=0.993, ESV r=0.992, EF r=0.930; overestimation 4 +/- 10 mL EDV, 1 +/- 9 mL ESV, 4 +/- 3% EF (all NS); reference database of 54 TOF patients; 19 +/- 3 landmark points entered. University of Washington (Sheehan); abstract does not name Ventripoint.

papers.title: Echocardiographic assessment of right ventricular volumes after surgical repair of tetralogy of Fallot: clinical validation of a new echocardiographic method.
papers.key_result: 2D-based 3D KBR (Ventripoint unit) vs cardiac MRI in 30 repaired-TOF patients (mean age 13.7 +/- 2.8 y); highly feasible with low intra/interobserver variability for EDV; 3D reconstruction underestimated RV volumes by 2.5% (EDV) and 4.6% (ESV) vs MRI.

papers.title: Echocardiographic assessment of right ventricular volumes: a comparison of different techniques in children after surgical repair of tetralogy of Fallot.
papers.key_result: KBR (3DR) feasibility 98%; underestimated EDV vs MRI by 6.6 ± 10 mL (MRI in 41 patients), better than 3D echo (18.2 ± 17.8 mL).

papers.title: Echocardiographic knowledge-based reconstruction for quantification of the systemic right ventricle in young adults with repaired D-transposition of great arteries.
papers.key_result: 2DE-KBR vs CMR: EDV r=0.80, ESV r=0.82, EF r=0.86; interobserver variability 4.6%/2.6%/4.3%.

papers.title: Three-dimensional modeling of the right ventricle from two-dimensional transthoracic echocardiographic images: utility of knowledge-based reconstruction in pulmonary arterial hypertension.
papers.key_result: KBR RV volumes vs CMR: EDV R=0.87, ESV R=0.88, EF R=0.75; interobserver CoV 7.8% EDV.

papers.title: Right ventricular volumes assessed by echocardiographic three-dimensional knowledge-based reconstruction compared with magnetic resonance imaging in a clinical setting.
papers.key_result: 30 TOF patients after PVR; feasibility 97%; correlation with MRI r=0.91 (EDV), 0.91 (ESV), 0.38 (EF); echo volumes significantly higher than MRI.

papers.title: Knowledge-based reconstruction of right ventricular volumes using real-time three-dimensional echocardiographic as well as cardiac magnetic resonance images: comparison with a cardiac magnetic resonance standard.
papers.key_result: KBR applied to RT3DE datasets vs CMR method-of-disks in 20 healthy + 40 CHD: EDV 1.1 ± 7.4% (r=0.990), EF 0.8 ± 9.2% (r=0.871); echo feasibility 88%. Abstract names only 'KBR software'; the Ventripoint vendor is not stated in the abstract.

papers.key_result: 2D KBR vs CMR bias ± LoA: EDV 3.5 ± 25.0 mL, ESV 0.9 ± 19.9 mL, EF 0.4 ± 10.2%; no significant test-retest differences.

papers.title: Knowledge-based 3D reconstruction of the right ventricle: comparison with cardiac magnetic resonance in adults with congenital heart disease.
papers.key_result: Reconstruction feasible in 16/19; RV volumes smaller than CMR (indexed EDV 114±17 vs 121±19 mL); ICC 0.84 EDV, 0.89 EF.

papers.title: Right Ventricular Assessment in Adult Congenital Heart Disease Patients with Right Ventricle-to-Pulmonary Artery Conduits.
papers.key_result: TTE-3DKBR (Ventripoint unit) vs CMR in 17 adults with RV-PA conduits: EDV R=0.77 (P=.0004), ESV R=0.93 (P<.0001), EF R=0.75 (P<.0005); CMR EDV slightly larger than 3DKBR, EF slightly higher by 3DKBR; RV shape diversity characterized on 43 separate CMR datasets.

papers.title: Two-dimensional knowledge-based volumetric reconstruction of the right ventricle documents short-term improvement in pulmonary hypertension.
papers.key_result: Longitudinal 2DKBR in 25 PH patients: RVEDVi 111±29 to 100±36 mL/m² (P=.038), RVEF 35±10% to 40±9% (P=.030) over 6.1 months; ESVi change correlated with NT-proBNP (r=-.77).

papers.title: Real-time 3D-echocardiography of the right ventricle-paediatric reference values for right ventricular volumes using knowledge-based reconstruction: a multicentre study.
papers.key_result: 545 healthy children (Philips iE33 / GE Vivid 7), VMS KBR analysis; adequate quality in 406/545 (74.5%); sex-specific BSA-indexed RV volume centiles; excellent intra/interobserver ICCs.

papers.title: Value of echocardiography using knowledge-based reconstruction in determining right ventricular volumes in pulmonary sarcoidosis: comparison with cardiac magnetic resonance imaging.
papers.key_result: TTE-KBR vs CMR: RVEDV bias 5.67 ± 55.4 mL (good); RVESV, RVSV and RVEF poor agreement (RVEF -12.9 ± 16.4%).

open_questions: K173810 summary reports no numeric performance results (bench testing only, no clinical study); no dataset sizes, sites, or accuracy figures for the LV/LA/RA catalogs.
Size and provenance of the KBR heart-model catalogs (training data) are not disclosed in the FDA summary or company pages.
Results of sponsor trials NCT01419756 (n=109) and NCT01557582 (n=103) were not located as publications in this session.

The peer-reviewed validations listed mostly concern the RV-only predicate VMS (K150628) with 2D-KBR and magnetic tracking; only Ahmad 2022 (software labelled VMS3.0+, LV/LA vs TomTec 3D) corresponds to the VMS+ 3.0 generation (K191493). No publication was found for VMS+ 4.0 or its AI first-guess feature.
K191493 reports bench testing only, with no numeric accuracy, dataset size or sites; it does not state whether the local KBR catalog is identical to the server-hosted catalog of K173810.

K241222: the AI point-placement algorithm is not described (model type, inputs, training data); the 160-image user study reports no proportions, number of users, patients or sites; and the summary states the accuracy of the AI initial points was not evaluated. Whether the feature covers all four chambers or only the RV (the study used RV images) is not stated.
K241222 states verification tests were performed 'against doctors' point placement' but no results are given.

openFDA lists the primary product code for K191493 as LLZ (the letter lists LLZ, IYN, IYO, ITX) and for K241222 as QIH (secondary LLZ); the product-code shift from IYN to LLZ/QIH across versions reflects reclassification as image-processing software rather than a change in function.
Vendor claim in the 2025-02-27 press release of 'accuracy equivalent to MRI' for VMS+ 4.0 is not supported by any study cited in that release or in K241222.

families.summary: FETOLY-HEART is an edge/on-device deep-learning application that receives the ultrasound video stream over HDMI and, in real time, detects the five ISUOG fetal cardiac screening views (abdomen, 4CH, LVOT, RVOT, 3VX) and 52 anatomical quality criteria within them, displaying exam completeness and an illustrative image set; users can override outputs. Cleared Sept 2024 (K241380) with Sonio Detect (K240406) predicate and GE SonoLystLive (K220358) reference, with a PCCP for retraining, hyperparameter changes and criteria addition/removal; standalone testing used 2,288 images from 480 cases at 7 U.S./French sites with per-view sensitivity 0.976-0.987 and specificity >=0.983. The successor FETOLY (K251368, 2025-09-12, predicate K241380, reference GE Voluson FETAL HS K220358, PCCP retained and extended) adds four fetal brain views with 43 criteria and automatic detection of measurement 'subviews' with eight biometric measurements, seven of them cardiac (cardiac axis, cardiothoracic ratio, TV/MV ventricular ratio, Ao/Du vessels ratio, vessel number, thymic-thoracic ratio, cardiothoracic position) plus cephalic index; completeness testing used 5,554 images/750 cases/7 sites (mean view sensitivity 96%, specificity 99.5%) and measurement testing 6,024 images/441 cases/6 sites (subview sensitivity 91.8%, specificity 99.9%; per-measurement limits of agreement reported).
families.intended_use_quote: FETOLY-HEART is intended to analyse fetal ultrasound images and clips using machine learning techniques to automatically detect heart views and quality criteria within the views. The device is intended for use as a concurrent reading aid during the acquisition and interpretation of fetal ultrasound images.

Fetoly-Heart is intended to analyze fetal ultrasound image sequences using machine learning techniques to automatically detect heart views and quality criteria within the views.
The device is intended for use as a concurrent reading aid during the acquisition and interpretation of fetal ultrasound images.
Fetoly-Heart is indicated for use during routine fetal heart examination of 2nd and 3rd trimester pregnancy (gestational age: from 17 to 40 weeks).

clearances.changes_summary: Initial clearance. Versus predicate Sonio Detect (cardiac features): 52 vs 28 quality criteria, local/edge platform vs cloud, adds automatic image extraction (covered by reference device, not predicate, SonoLystLive in Voluson Expert 22/20/18, K220358), GE/Samsung/Canon compatibility (predicate also Philips). PCCP: retraining with new data, hyperparameter changes, addition/removal of heart quality criteria within the 5 views.

FETOLY (trade name drops '-HEART'). Predicate FETOLY-HEART (K241380); reference device FETAL HS feature in GE Voluson Expert 22/20/18 (K220358) for automatic biometric measurements. Same edge/HDMI platform, GE/Samsung/Canon compatibility, user override, and 5 heart views/52 criteria. Adds: 4 fetal brain views with 43 quality criteria; ML detection of measurement subviews (M1-M8) and automatic biometric measurements with normal-range display (7 cardiac + cephalic index); measurement illustrations and an exportable exam report. PCCP cleared covering retraining with new training/validation data, hyperparameter changes, heart/brain quality-criteria addition/removal and addition of new biometric measurements, with new models tested for superiority on a held-out test set. open_questions: Training/validation dataset size and sites for model development are not disclosed.
Numeric subgroup results (by site, BMI, scanner, race, image quality, cardiac abnormality) are stated to have been analyzed but not reported.
Whether the 4.2% Canon share (20 cases) is sufficient to support the Canon compatibility claim is not addressed.
Hardware platform in K241380 ('hardware device ... connected through an HDMI connection', 'Tablet compatibility testing') is not named; company site lists iPad and Samsung Galaxy Tab models.
No ClinicalTrials.gov registration found for Diagnoly/FETOLY.
Turan 2026 (J Ultrasound Med) uses report still images rather than the real-time stream; its link to the cleared algorithm version is unstated.

K251368 reports only pooled mean sensitivity/specificity/IoU across views and criteria; per-view and per-criterion results (available in K241380) are not given, so cardiac-view performance of FETOLY cannot be compared view-by-view with FETOLY-HEART.
K251368 LOA values are single numbers without units, sign, or definition (half-width vs bound), and the predetermined per-measurement acceptance thresholds are not stated; bias is not reported.

K251368 text says cases were collected 'until ... an overall of 310 patient files were reached' for studies that report 750 and 441 cases; the relation between the 310 planning minimum and the final counts is not explained.
Whether the 52 cardiac quality-criteria model in FETOLY is identical to the FETOLY-HEART model or was retrained under the PCCP is not stated.

The company product page lists cerebral ventricle-to-hemisphere and CSP length-to-width ratios that do not appear among the eight cleared measurements in K251368; whether these were added under the PCCP is unknown.

No clinical (reader or workflow) study is reported in either clearance; impact on detection of congenital heart disease (HLHS, coarctation, TGA named on the product page) is not evaluated in the FDA summaries.

The 52-criteria lists differ in labelling between K241380 (Table 1, pp.6-7) and K251368 (Table 1, pp.7-8): abdomen A8 'Thorax apex' became 'Anterior Abdomen'; 4CH B9 'Foramen Ovale flap (Vieussens valve)' became 'Septum primum (Vieussens valve or Foramen Ovale Flap)'; 3VX E4/E5 'Main pulmonary artery'/'Ductus (Ductal arch)' became 'Ductal arch connected to the descending aorta'/'Ductal arch not connected to the descending aorta'. Whether these are relabelled or retrained criteria is not stated.

families.product_name: Aplio i-series and a-series cardiac AI features (2D WMT with Full-assist, Auto EF with Full-assist, Auto Plane Detection, Quick Strain, Auto LVOT, Auto AoV); UltraExtend NX offline workstation
families.summary: Canon's Aplio i900/i800/i700 cardiac AI functions comprise AI/ML-supported automated initial left-ventricular contour tracing for 2D Wall Motion Tracking and Auto EF (marketed as 'Full-assist', labeled as AI/ML-supported in K212333 (i-series) and K212960 (a-series) as a marketing-language expansion of previously cleared features), and four features added in K241582 (software V7.0) that the summary validates as 'improved AI/ML based features': Auto Plane Detection (deep-learning A4C/A2C/A3C/SAX view selection for 2D WMT), Quick Strain (a workflow feature that uses Auto Plane Detection to run 2D WMT LV simultaneously on three apical views yielding EDV, ESV, EF, GLS), Auto LVOT and Auto AoV (deep-learning tracing of LVOT and AV Doppler waveforms). K241582 validated these on sequestered data from 239 U.S. patients at one site (subsets of 50/50/45/45 patients) against three sonographers; K250328 cleared the UltraExtend NX V2.0 offline workstation carrying 2D WMT Full-assist and Auto EF Full-assist migrated unchanged from K223017, with no numeric results reported; the summary states only that both features 'perform as intended' with substantial equivalence to the reference device. K212960 (Aplio a550/a450/a Software V6.5, 2022-03-22, predicate K202364) is the a-series counterpart of K212333: it proposes the same AI/ML marketing-language expansion for the previously cleared automated initial contour tracing of 2D WMT (LV) and Auto EF (LV) ('Full-assist'), lists a non-AI SmartFetal2D improvement to fetal-heart 2D WMT, and reports only phantom/volunteer testing of improved features with no AI performance data and no clinical study.
families.indications_for_use_quote: The Diagnostic Ultrasound System Aplio i900 Model TUS-AI900, Aplio i800 Model TUS-AI800, and Aplio i700 Model TUS-AI700 are indicated for the visualization of structures, and dynamic processes with the human body using ultrasound and to provide image information for diagnosis in the following clinical applications: fetal, abdominal, intra-operative (abdominal), pediatric, small organs (thyroid, breast and testicle), trans-vaginal, trans-rectal, neonatal cephalic, adult cephalic, cardiac (both adult and pediatric), peripheral vascular, transesophageal, musculo-skeletal (both conventional and superficial), laparoscopic and Thoracic/Pleural. This system provides high-quality ultrasound images in the following modes: B mode, M mode, Continuous Wave, Color Doppler, Pulsed Wave Doppler, Power Doppler and Combination Doppler, as well as Speckle-tracking, Tissue Harmonic Imaging, Combined Modes, Shear wave, Elastography, and Acoustic attenuation mapping. This system is suitable for use in hospital and clinical settings by physicians or legally qualified persons who have received the appropriate training.

training_data.description: K241582 states only that test data were 'entirely independent and sequestered from the data used for training'; no training set size, source, or site count is given for any feature. K212333 and K250328 give no training information. K212960 gives no training information.

validation_data.description: Images from 239 demographically diverse patients acquired over a two-month period at a U.S. clinical site; test data entirely independent and sequestered from training data; acquired with predicate device (Aplio i-series V7.0). Ground truth by three licensed clinical sonographers. Feature-level test subsets: Auto Plane Detection 50 patients; Quick Strain 50; Auto LVOT 45; Auto AoV 45. K250328: representative subset of the original K223017 validation data (size not stated). K212333: no validation data described. K212960: phantom and volunteer testing only, no sizes, no AI-feature-specific data.

prior_validations.description: K250328 states that 2D WMT Full-assist (LV) and Auto EF Full-assist (LV) were originally validated with clinical data under reference device K223017 (Aplio i-series V7.0, cleared 2023-03-31); that summary was not part of this batch and its results were not read.

Canon US cardiology page repeats the K241582 figures (Quick Strain 97% plane recognition accuracy and 68% time reduction; Auto Plane Detection 97% accuracy) and adds an Auto AoV 82% keystroke-reduction claim.

papers.title: Accuracy and reliability of novel semi-automated two-dimensional layer specific speckle tracking software for quantifying left ventricular volumes and function
papers.key_result: Canon Aplio 300 (PST-30BT) with a vendor-dependent PROTOTYPE automated contour trace (ACT) layer-strain software (co-author Abe is a Canon employee; Takeuchi received a Canon equipment grant), not the cleared Full-assist feature: 84 patients with same-day CMR; software failed in 3 (feasibility 96%); coverage probability for LVEF vs CMR disk-area summation 0.77 endocardial, 0.75 mid-myocardial, 0.58 epicardial (full text, PMC6716624); GLS CP vs CMR feature tracking 0.95 (mid) vs 0.92 (endo); intra-observer ICC 0.991 (LVEF) and 0.989 (GLS) with endocardial tracking.

papers.title: Effect of cross-platform variations on transthoracic echocardiography measurements and clinical diagnosis
papers.journal: European Heart Journal - Imaging Methods and Practice
papers.key_result: Cross-vendor comparison of Philips EPIQ CVx 9.0.3 vs Canon Aplio i900 V7.0 in 40 healthy volunteers (single centre; partly funded by a Canon Medical Systems USA contract). Canon Auto EF was used for single-plane A2C/A4C volume calculations on the Canon system but was not itself evaluated against a reference; Canon single-plane LVEF 61.68 +/- 6.32% vs Philips 60.40 +/- 7.97% (p=0.19); Canon biplane LVEF 60.06 +/- 8.50%.

papers.title: Vendor differences in 2D-speckle tracking global longitudinal strain: an update on a 10-year standardization effort
papers.key_result: Six-vendor GLS comparison (372 exams, 62 subjects, LVEF 30-68%) including Canon vendor-specific semi-automated strain software: contemporary semi-automated clinical software (GE, Philips, Canon, Fujifilm, Caas Qardia) showed average maximum inter-vendor bias of 0.6% strain units; minimal detectable change 2.5/2.4 strain% (endocardial/mid-wall); GLS test-retest variability 6.6% vs 6.5% for LVEF. Canon system model, software version and whether the Full-assist function was used are not stated in the abstract.

open_questions: Training data size, source, and number of sites are not disclosed for any of the six AI features in K212333, K241582, or K250328.

K212333 states 2D WMT Full-assist and Auto EF Full-assist were 'previously 510(k) cleared' but does not name the original clearance; the earliest K carrying the automated contour tracing is unknown (predicate K201972, V5.1, not read).

Numeric performance of 2D WMT Full-assist and Auto EF Full-assist is not reported in any included summary; K250328 attributes the original validation to reference device K223017 (Aplio i-series V7.0, 2023-03-31), which is outside this batch.
K241582 reports ICC(2,1) and NRMSE only as thresholds met (>0.75, <10%); exact values, bias, and per-view agreement percentages for Auto Plane Detection are not given.
K241582 validation is single-site (one U.S. clinical site); generalizability beyond that site is not tested.
K250328 does not state whether Auto Plane Detection, Quick Strain, Auto LVOT, or Auto AoV are available in UltraExtend NX V2.0; only the two Full-assist features are named.

No peer-reviewed validation of the cleared Full-assist, Quick Strain, Auto Plane Detection, Auto LVOT, or Auto AoV features was found via PubMed this session; the Kitano 2019 paper evaluates a Canon prototype ACT software, not the cleared feature.
Vendor claim of 82% keystroke reduction for Auto AoV has no counterpart in the FDA summary and its study basis is not described.

Whether the Aplio a-series, Aplio beyond/me (K253597), and V8.x/V9.0 Aplio i-series (K233195, K242808, K252074) carry these cardiac AI features unchanged is not stated in the included summaries. The Canon US cardiology page (company source) footnotes Auto EF as available on 'Aplio i-series / Prism Edition and a-series' but the AI Full-assist function, Doppler AI, Quick Strain and Auto Plane Detection as 'Aplio i-series / Prism Edition only'.

Canon-hosted clinical report 'Objective Echocardiography with Superior Reproducibility Based on Artificial Intelligence Technology' (Tokushima University, Kusunose) appears in web search results but the URL returned 404; a PubMed search of Kusunose K AI-echocardiography papers found only Us2.ai-based or non-Canon studies, so its relation to the cleared features is unconfirmed.
K212960 (a-series V6.5), like K212333, states 2D WMT Full-assist and Auto EF Full-assist were 'previously 510(k) cleared' without naming the clearance; predicate K202364 (a-series V5.1) was not read.

K212960 does not state whether the a-series Full-assist algorithms are identical to the i-series implementation; the Canon US cardiology page (company source) lists Auto EF for a-series but the AI Full-assist function for 'Aplio i-series / Prism Edition only', which is in tension with the K212960 marketing-language expansion.

K212960 lists 'SmartFetal2D' (2D WMT for fetal heart, candidate heart-cycle selection) as an improvement without describing it as AI; its relation, if any, to the adult cardiac AI features is unknown.
